subject: CardioAI: request for canary pin + auto-fallback as SLA mitigation
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@cardio.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting canary pin + auto-fallback as SLA safeguard for planned cutover

Olga —

We’re planning a production model swap next week (v3.1 -> v4.0) to improve clinical throughput. Our SREs are asking for a conservative canary with an automatic fallback and an option to pin the previous model if latency or error rates climb. Given CardioAI’s uptime SLA (99.95% + P95 latency target < 180ms), we want to avoid any blips during the migration window.

Can Redwood authorize a temporary canary policy that: 
- routes 5% traffic to v4.0 for 30 minutes,
- enables an automatic fallback to v3.1 when error-rate > 0.5% OR P95 latency > 220ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows,
- allows CardioAI to request a manual pin for up to 24 hours if we observe anomalous behavior (with acceptance from Redwood on emergency steps),
- documents the rollback steps (we attached the plan).

We’re happy to accept a short SLO credit carveout while the canary runs, but need formal ok from Redwood so our procurement and legal teams can sign off.

Attachments: cardio_canary_plan_v2.pdf

—Ben
Ben Wallace
Head of Platform Engineering, CardioAI
ben.wallace@cardio.ai

Subject: Re: Requesting canary pin + auto-fallback as SLA safeguard for planned cutover

Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan and the attachment. I’ll start the internal approval flow. High level: Redwood can support an automated canary with the fallback thresholds you suggested, but we need engineering sign-off on the autorevert timers and product approval for any temporary SLA carveout language. Can you confirm the expected traffic pattern (steady vs diurnal burst) during your 30-minute window and whether you want streaming sessions included in the 5% canary or only discrete generation requests?

I’m looping in our Product (Laura) and Platform (Marcus) to evaluate the risk and operational controls. Please keep the SREs on stand-by — we may ask for an additional short smoke test prior to the full canary.

Attachment received and forwarded to our ops reviewers.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: CardioAI canary exception request — ask for authorizations

Team —

CardioAI (CardioAI) is requesting a formal exception to our standard rollout policy for a 5% canary with auto-fallback and an ability to pin a previous model for up to 24 hours. They are offering to accept a limited SLO credit while the canary runs. Key asks:
- Autorevert trigger: error-rate > 0.5% OR P95 latency > 220ms for two consecutive 5-minute windows (they propose),
- Autorevert action: immediate routing of all traffic back to pinned v3.1; KV cache warmup to be handled automatically by the runtime,
- Manual pin: CardioAI can initiate a manual pin (service request) which Redwood will honor within agreed change window (we should define the execution SLA),
- Smoke test: 5 minute canary dry-run prior to public roll,
- Observability: full tracing + token-level latency during canary, plus a short post-mortem commit.

Attachments: cardio_canary_plan_v2.pdf, canary_runbook_v3.pdf (included below).

Please review the following risk considerations and comment with any changes:
1) Autorevert window length — Marcus, if autorevert happens quickly it minimizes end-user impact but increases the chance of flip-flopping for transient spikes. Suggest we make autorevert require two consecutive windows and a 2-minute cool-down before attempting a re-apply.
2) Pinning policy — we should allow a manual pin for up to 24 hours; any longer requires an RFC and account billing/credit approval.
3) SLA carveout — Product needs to propose language (percentage/timebox) and Finance must approve whether a credit applies.

Required approvals: Engineering (Marcus), Product (Laura), and Ops (SRE liaison). Marcus — can you confirm the autorevert implementation and the expected rollback latency? Laura — can you propose the carveout language we can present to CardioAI and legal?

Thanks,
Olga

[attachment: cardio_canary_plan_v2.pdf]
[attachment: canary_runbook_v3.pdf]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@cardio.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CardioAI canary exception request — ask for authorizations

Olga / Laura —

Reviewed the runbook and the thresholds. Engineering supports the requested autorevert behavior with a couple of constraints: 
- Implementation: We will implement the autorevert as an automated routing rule tied to the telemetry pipeline. If the P95 or error-rate condition is met for two consecutive 5-minute buckets, the control plane will switch all traffic to pinned v3.1 within ~40–90 seconds (depends on KV cache warmup for streaming sessions).
- Flap protection: We'll add a 2-minute cool-down post-autorevert before any automated re-try; manual re-deploys remain possible with Ops oversight.
- Pin execution SLA: Manual pin requests from CardioAI will be executed within 15 minutes during business hours (we'll queue out-of-hours requests and notify).
- SLA carveout: Product will need to scope the credit. Engineering recommends limiting automatic carveouts to the canary window only (30m) — longer pins trigger formal review.

Given these guardrails, I authorize this exception from an engineering standpoint. Please surface Product/legal wording for the temporary SLA treatment and we can proceed with a coordinated dry-run.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
